source: Web research pass (Aug 2026): 25+ primary sources — docs.wpilib.org (stable + latest/2027), docs.advantagekit.org, github.com/wpilibsuite (allwpilib, vendor-json-repo, vendor-template, frc-docs, GradleRIO), github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit (template_projects), github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public, github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib, github.com/FRCTeam2910/2026CompetitionRobot-Public, github.com/Spectrum3847/2026-Spectrum, docs.yagsl.com + live yagsl.json, doglog.dev, docs.revrobotics.com, api.ctr-electronics.com, maven.photonvision.org (live 2027-alpha vendordep), github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim. NOTE: chiefdelphi.com returned HTTP 403 to every fetch attempt, so no Chief Delphi thread content is quoted first-hand below; CD claims are flagged as unverified.
summary: The FRC ecosystem has converged on one dominant architecture — a hardware-abstraction "IO layer" (interface + auto-logged inputs struct + one impl per vendor + a sim impl) sitting under a thin logic-only subsystem — pioneered by 6328's AdvantageKit and now used verbatim by 254, 3061, and most published 2025/2026 codebases (https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/io-interfaces/). Nobody has solved the boilerplate problem: the same pattern costs 4-6 files per mechanism, and the two credible mitigations in the wild are (a) a *generic* configurable base class — 254's `ServoMotorSubsystem<T extends MotorInputsAutoLogged, U extends MotorIO>` with a plain mutable `ServoMotorSubsystemConfig` that just wraps `TalonFXConfiguration` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public/main/src/main/java/com/team254/lib/subsystems/ServoMotorSubsystemConfig.java), and (b) Spectrum 3847's `Mechanism.Config` subclass-and-call-`configX()` pattern with Lombok `@Getter` (https://github.com/Spectrum3847/2026-Spectrum). Notably, neither uses a true fluent builder — vendors do (`SparkMaxConfig` chaining, Phoenix 6 `withSlot0()/withMotionMagic()`), teams don't; teams instead subclass a mutable config and call void `config*()` setters, and the most-copied WPILib/AdvantageKit templates still use flat `public static final double` files (`DriveConstants.java`) that fundamentally cannot express two elevators. Config-as-data (YAGSL's `deploy/swerve/*.json`) buys one-line construction and per-robot directories at the cost of compile-time safety and a documented "you will likely never get it working on the first try" debugging experience (https://docs.yagsl.com/configuring-yagsl/configuration/swerve-module-configuration). The distribution story is now fully pinned down: the authoritative vendordep schema lives in `check.py` in wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo (required: fileName/name/version/uuid/mavenUrls/jsonUrl/java+jni+cppDependencies; optional: `frcYear` OR `wpilibYear` — exactly one — plus `requires`/`conflictsWith`), a pure-Java library needs zero JNI and can ship off JitPack (DogLog does exactly this) or a GitHub-Pages static Maven repo (YAGSL does), and GitHub Packages is disqualified because its Maven registry requires a token even for public artifacts. The single biggest strategic input: 2027 is a hard break — `edu.wpi.first` → `org.wpilib`, Java 25, roboRIO → SystemCore (`linuxsystemcore` platform), Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard/PathWeaver/RobotBuilder deleted, and a brand-new Commands v3 built on Java continuations whose core noun is literally `Mechanism` — meaning a library designed now should target the v3 mechanism model rather than entrench v2 `SubsystemBase`.
stack:
TARGET YEARS — 2026 (concluded season, REBUILT): WPILib 2026.2.x, JDK 17, roboRIO 2, `edu.wpi.first.*` packages, command-based v2, Units/Measure API (`edu.wpi.first.units`), Epilogue `@Logged`. 2027 (upcoming, alpha-5 as of Aug 2026): WPILib 2027.0.0-alpha-4/5, **Java 25 + C++23 required**, packages renamed `edu.wpi.first` → `org.wpilib` (C++ `frc::` → `wpi::`), **SystemCore replaces roboRIO** (new platform triple `linuxsystemcore`; Motioncore; multiple CAN buses, Smart IO, onboard IMU, Expansion Hub), Gradle 9.4.1 + ZGC default, Jackson → Avaje Jsonb, NT3 removed, `robotInit()` removed, "Test" mode renamed "Utility", `MotorController::set()` → `setThrottle()`, gamepad classes collapsed into one `Gamepad`, Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard/PathWeaver/RobotBuilder **discontinued**, Commands v3 (`org.wpilib.commands3`) added alongside deprecated-in-place v2 (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html). Confirmed live 2027-alpha artifacts exist for AdvantageKit (27.0.0-alpha-4), PathplannerLib, Phoenix6 (26.50.0-alpha-1), REVLib, ThriftyLib, photonlib, DogLog, AmLib (https://github.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo/tree/main/2027_alpha5).
MOTOR CONTROLLERS / SENSORS in published team code: CTRE TalonFX (Kraken/Falcon 500) + TalonFXS + CANdi + CANcoder + Pigeon 2 + CANivore (254, 3061, 2910, Spectrum 3847); REV SPARK MAX / SPARK Flex + NEO / NEO 550 / Neo Vortex (AdvantageKit spark_swerve template); Redux, ThriftyLib, Studica/navX as secondary vendors. AdvantageKit ships *two* swerve templates precisely because CTRE and REV split the field.
FRAMEWORKS IN USE: AdvantageKit (IO + replay), DogLog (simple logging, Team 581), Epilogue (`@Logged`, WPILib first-party), PathPlanner + Choreo, PhotonVision/Limelight, maple-sim (dyn4j-backed physics sim, 2026 release tracks WPILib 2026.2.1), YAGSL (JSON swerve), 3061-lib (swerve starter), Lombok + Spotless + SpotBugs (Spectrum 3847 build tooling).

patterns.name: AdvantageKit IO-layer pattern (the de facto FRC standard)
patterns.whatItDoes: Splits every mechanism into three layers: (1) public command/API surface, (2) control logic, (3) hardware interface. The cut between 2 and 3 is a Java interface `XIO` containing an `@AutoLog`-annotated static inner class `XIOInputs` of plain public fields, plus `updateInputs(inputs)` and a set of `default`-implemented command methods. An annotation processor generates `XIOInputsAutoLogged` with `toLog()`/`fromLog()`. The subsystem holds `private final XIO io` (constructor-injected) and one `XIOInputsAutoLogged inputs`, and every `periodic()` starts with `io.updateInputs(inputs); Logger.processInputs("Name", inputs);`. Swapping `XIOSim`/`XIOTalonFX`/`XIOSpark` at the RobotContainer level changes nothing above the line. Docs explicitly note all IO methods should have default impls so a sim/blank IO is a one-liner, and that the input cache is deliberately never updated mid-cycle so all readers see identical values within a loop.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/io-interfaces/ ; verbatim source https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/main/template_projects/sources/talonfx_swerve/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/drive/ModuleIO.java and .../spark_swerve/.../Module.java ; adopted by Team 254 (every 2025 subsystem, https://github.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public), Team 3061 (https://github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib), Team 2554 docs (https://docs.jpsrobotics2554.org/programming/advanced-concepts/AdvantageKit-and-IO-Layers/)
patterns.libraryValue: This is the pattern PumpkinLib must be compatible with, not fight. The highest-leverage move is to SHIP the IO interface + inputs record + sim impl for common mechanism archetypes (elevator, pivot/arm, roller/flywheel, turret) so a small team writes zero IO files. Note the file layout is 100% mechanical and derivable from a config — it is code-generation-shaped. Also note the Alert integration: the template pairs each `xConnected` boolean input with a `new Alert("Disconnected drive motor…", AlertType.kError)` toggled in periodic — free hardware-fault UX a library should bake in.

patterns.name: Team 254 generic ServoMotorSubsystem + delegating config object
patterns.whatItDoes: A single generic base class `ServoMotorSubsystem<T extends MotorInputsAutoLogged, U extends MotorIO>` covers ALL position/velocity mechanisms. It exposes command factories rather than raw setters: `dutyCycleCommand()`, `voltageCommand()`, `positionSetpointCommand()`, `motionMagicSetpointCommand()`, `velocitySetpointCommand()`, `setTorqueCurrentFOC()`, `setCoast()`, plus blocking variants built as `.until(<within tolerance>)`. The config object is deliberately *dumb*: a plain class of public mutable fields that does NOT re-model PID/motion-magic at all — it embeds the vendor's own `TalonFXConfiguration` and adds only the four things the vendor object can't express (name, CAN id, unit↔rotor ratio, min/max position, sim MOI). A `ServoMotorSubsystemWithFollowers` variant handles leader/follower. Concrete mechanisms (ElevatorSubsystem) extend it, call `super(...)`, and override only `setMotionMagicSetpointImpl()` / `periodic()` to add domain logic (hall-effect homing, range-sensor stow, debounced gyro trigger).
patterns.whereSeen: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Team254/FRC-2025-Public/main/src/main/java/com/team254/lib/subsystems/ServoMotorSubsystemConfig.java ; ServoMotorSubsystem.java and frc2025/subsystems/elevator/ElevatorSubsystem.java in the same repo ; package split documented in README: com.team254.frc2025.* (robot) vs com.team254.lib.* (reusable)
patterns.libraryValue: This is the single best template for PumpkinLib's core abstraction, and its most important lesson is NEGATIVE SPACE: do not re-invent gains/current-limits/soft-limits — embed the vendor config object and add only the ~5 fields it lacks. That is why the whole config class is 12 lines. Also copy the command-factory-not-setter surface: a small team writes `elevator.motionMagicSetpointCommand(L4)` and never touches a PIDController. The generic <Inputs, IO> parameterization is how you get one base class to serve TalonFX, Spark, and sim.

patterns.name: Spectrum 3847 Mechanism.Config — subclass + void config*() setters (NOT a fluent builder)
patterns.whatItDoes: An abstract `Mechanism` base wrapping TalonFX leader+followers, with a nested `public static class Config` that each mechanism SUBCLASSES. The subclass constructor calls a vocabulary of ~25 void helpers: `configPIDGains(kP,kI,kD)`, `configPIDGains(slot,…)`, `configFeedForwardGains(kS,kV,kA,kG)`, `configMotionMagic(cruiseVel,accel,jerk)`, `configGearRatio(r)` (writes `Feedback.SensorToMechanismRatio`), `configForwardSoftLimit(threshold,enabled)`, `configReverseSoftLimit(…)`, `configSupplyCurrentLimit(a,enabled)`, `configStatorCurrentLimit(…)`, `configGravityType(isArm)` (Arm_Cosine vs Elevator_Static), `configContinuousWrap(b)`, `configNeutralBrakeMode(b)`, `configMinMaxRotations(min,max)`, `configFeedbackSensorSource(src,offset)`. Every helper just mutates the embedded `TalonFXConfiguration`. Lombok `@Getter`/`@Setter` erase accessor boilerplate. Control request objects (`MotionMagicVoltage`, `MotionMagicTorqueCurrentFOC`, `VelocityVoltage`, `TorqueCurrentFOC`, `DutyCycleOut`…) are pre-allocated ONCE as config fields and reused every loop with fluent `.with*()` — explicit GC-pressure avoidance. `Config#isAttached()==false` puts the mechanism in software-only mode returning safe defaults — a first-class "this mechanism isn't on the robot yet" switch. Sensor reads go through a `CachedDouble` that updates at most once per periodic loop to bound CAN traffic. Mechanism state is expressed as `Trigger` factories (position/velocity/current thresholds), which the team says "all but eliminates the need for complex multi-mechanism command groups."
patterns.libraryValue: Strongest evidence about what teams ACTUALLY tolerate: a mature team library chose imperative void setters over a fluent builder, because config subclassing composes with inheritance and lets you set defaults in the base constructor (they disable hardware limit switches by default there). The `isAttached()` flag, the `CachedDouble` once-per-loop read, and pre-allocated control requests are three concrete, copyable ergonomics wins for PumpkinLib. Their layout (framework/, hardware/, mechanism/, sim/, swerve/, telemetry/, util/, vision/, leds/, gamepads/) is a ready-made package skeleton for a team-agnostic library.

patterns.name: Team 3061 abstract RobotConfig — one subclass per physical robot
patterns.whatItDoes: An abstract `RobotConfig` class declares every robot-varying value as abstract getters (CAN IDs, `FRONT_LEFT_MODULE_STEER_OFFSET_ROT`, `AUTO_DRIVE_P_CONTROLLER`, etc). A `RobotType` enum in `Constants.java` selects the concrete subclass at startup: ROBOT_DEFAULT→`DefaultRobotConfig`, ROBOT_COMPETITION→`CompetitionRobotConfig`, PRACTICE_BOARD→…, VISION_TEST_PLATFORM→…, ROBOT_SIMBOT→sim. Adding a robot = adding one subclass. Paired with a global `TUNING_MODE` boolean in Constants.java that flips tunable numbers live under the `/Tuning` NetworkTables path readable/writable from AdvantageScope, so PID changes need no redeploy. Explicitly motivated by: practice bot vs comp bot, testing one isolated mechanism, and vision-only test platforms.
patterns.whereSeen: https://github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib/blob/main/README.md ; parallel implementation in FRC 2910's `config/` package ("contains robot configuration framework and constants specific to each robot") https://github.com/FRCTeam2910/2026CompetitionRobot-Public/ ; Spectrum 3847's `frc/robot/configs/` with FM2026/XM2026/PM2026/AM2026/PHOTON2026 variants
patterns.libraryValue: Multi-robot support is a top-3 real need and every serious team solves it with polymorphism, not files. For PumpkinLib this argues for making the mechanism config a first-class VALUE that can be produced by a per-robot factory/enum, rather than static constants. The 'test platform' and 'isolated mechanism bench' robot types are the small-team superpower here — a small team's practice bot is usually a bench with one mechanism on it, and this pattern makes that a one-line switch.

patterns.name: Vendor fluent/nested config objects — the only true builders in FRC
patterns.whatItDoes: Both major vendors converged on fluent config in 2025. REV: `SparkMaxConfig` chains top-level setters and exposes NESTED sub-config objects (`config.encoder.countsPerRevolution(8192).inverted(true)`), applied atomically via `spark.configure(config, ResetMode.kResetSafeParameters, PersistMode.kPersistParameters)` — where `kResetSafeParameters` resets everything writable except CAN ID/Motor Type/Idle Mode/PWM deadband/duty-cycle offset first, so config is declarative-total rather than incremental. CTRE Phoenix 6: `TalonFXConfiguration` exposes `withSlot0(...)`, `withMotionMagic(...)` etc, each documented as returning `this` "for method-chaining and easier to use config API"; sub-configs are also plain public fields (`talonConfig.Slot0.kP = 0.11`), so both styles work.
patterns.libraryValue: Two things to steal. (1) The ResetMode idea: 'apply this config and reset everything else to known defaults' is what makes hardware config reproducible after a motor swap — a huge small-team failure mode. PumpkinLib should default to total/declarative apply, never incremental. (2) Nested sub-config namespaces (`.encoder`, `.closedLoop`, `.softLimit`) beat a flat 40-method builder for discoverability. But note the ecosystem reality: teams do NOT wrap these in their own builders — they embed the vendor config object whole (254, Spectrum). Wrapping every vendor knob is a losing maintenance race.

patterns.name: Config-as-data: YAGSL JSON swerve configuration
patterns.whatItDoes: The entire drivetrain is described by JSON in `src/main/deploy/swerve/`: `swervedrive.json` (imu {type,id,canbus}, invertedIMU, modules[] listing module files in clockwise order from front-left), `controllerproperties.json`, `physicalproperties.json`, `pidfproperties.json`, and `modules/frontleft.json|frontright.json|backleft.json|backright.json`. Construction is genuinely one line. YAGSL's stated pros: swap robots by swapping a config directory; 'your constants file doesn't have to take 10 minutes to find the right option'; same code across robots. YAGSL's own docs state the con plainly: configuring a module 'requires a lot of patience and you will likely never get it working on the first try' and 'if one of these configuration values are not set correctly you might experience behavior that you won't easily be able to identify.' Community mitigation is a curated repo of known-good configs per COTS module.
patterns.libraryValue: The honest read: JSON's win is the CONFIG DIRECTORY per robot and shippable presets, not the file format. PumpkinLib can capture both wins without giving up the compiler — ship typed preset constants (`Presets.MAXSwerve`, `Presets.MK4i_L2`) as Java values, and make the per-robot switch a class/enum (3061 pattern). If config-as-data is wanted anyway, the mitigations the ecosystem proves necessary are: (a) validate the whole config at construction and fail loud with the offending file+key, (b) ship a preset library, (c) a deploy-dir file is invisible to `git diff` review in a way a .java file is not. Also note deploy-dir JSON does NOT round-trip into AdvantageKit replay unless logged as an input.

patterns.name: WPILib Units (Measure) API for type-safe mechanism config
patterns.whatItDoes: `edu.wpi.first.units` (2027: `org.wpilib.units`) gives dimension-checked values: `Distance wheelDiameter = Inches.of(6)`, `LinearVelocity maxSpeed = FeetPerSecond.of(12.5)`, `Mass armMass = Kilograms.of(1.423)`, `Angle maxTravel = Rotations.of(0.45)`. Arithmetic is typed — `Distance.divide(Time)` yields `LinearVelocity`; `maxSpeed.in(RadiansPerSecond)` is a COMPILE error. Composite units without subclassing: `PerUnit<VoltageUnit,DistanceUnit> voltsPerInch = Volts.per(Inches)`. WPILib's own explicit API-design guidance: methods should ACCEPT `Measure` but RETURN concrete immutable types (`Distance`, not `MutDistance`) so callers can't mutate internals; and `.in()` should only be used 'when interacting with APIs that do not support the units library.' `MutableMeasure`/`MutDistance` exist purely for GC avoidance in hot loops via `mut_replace/mut_plus/mut_minus`, with a loud warning that mutating changes the value everywhere the instance is referenced.
patterns.libraryValue: Units are the single best fit for 'an elevator with these gains, this gearing, these soft limits' because they kill the #1 small-team bug class — meters vs inches vs rotations vs radians in a constants file. Config objects are CONSTRUCTION-TIME, not hot-loop, so the GC caveat does not apply to config and you can use immutable `Measure` freely there. AdvantageKit's `@AutoLogOutput` already understands `Measure` and emits unit metadata for AdvantageScope's unit-aware graphing (2026 feature) — so a Units-first PumpkinLib gets correct dashboard axes for free. Rule to adopt verbatim: accept `Measure` in signatures, return concrete immutable types, never expose a Mut* type.

patterns.name: Java records as config + StructGenerator.genRecord for free serialization/logging
patterns.whatItDoes: WPILib ships `StructGenerator.genRecord(Class<R extends Record>)` returning a `Struct<R>`, plus `genEnum(Class<E>)` and `addCustomStruct(clazz, struct, override)` — i.e. a record-shaped config object becomes NT/WPILOG-serializable with one static line, no hand-written schema. `StructSerializable` is the marker interface; anything implementing it (or with a registered Struct) is loggable by AdvantageKit `@AutoLogOutput` and by Epilogue. If generation fails, WPILib prints the errors and returns a no-op Struct rather than throwing.
patterns.libraryValue: This closes the loop on 'config as typed data': define `ElevatorConfig` as a record, add `public static final Struct<ElevatorConfig> struct = StructGenerator.genRecord(ElevatorConfig.class)`, and the exact configuration a robot ran with is logged into the WPILOG and visible in AdvantageScope — which is the config-as-data benefit (introspectable, diffable, per-robot) WITHOUT giving up compile-time checking. Records also give free equals/hashCode/toString, canonical constructors for validation (throw in a compact constructor on maxHeight<minHeight), and `withX()` copy methods are trivial to hand-write for modification. CAVEAT I could not verify: I found no doc enumerating which field types genRecord supports, and no doc confirming `Measure`-typed record components serialize — assume plain doubles/enums/nested records are safe and TEST before relying on Measure inside a struct record.

patterns.name: Sealed interfaces for exhaustive mechanism/hardware variants (DESIGN PROPOSAL — not observed in FRC)
patterns.whatItDoes: Sealed interfaces (Java 17, JEP 409) + pattern-matching switch (Java 21, JEP 441) let you declare a closed set of alternatives the compiler checks exhaustively — e.g. `sealed interface MotorSpec permits TalonFXSpec, SparkSpec, SimSpec`, then `switch (spec) { case TalonFXSpec t -> new TalonFXIO(t); case SparkSpec s -> new SparkIO(s); case SimSpec m -> new SimIO(m); }` with no default branch and a compile error when a new vendor is added and a site is missed.
patterns.whereSeen: Language feature: JEP 409/441; general Java writeups e.g. https://neilmadden.blog/2026/04/24/java-sealed-classes-and-exhaustive-pattern-matching/ . EXPLICITLY UNVERIFIED IN FRC: I searched and could NOT find any published FRC team library or vendor library using sealed interfaces for subsystem/hardware modeling. Treat this as an unexploited opportunity, not an imitable precedent. Java version support is fine: WPILib 2026 requires JDK 17 (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/zero-to-robot/step-2/wpilib-setup.html), and 2027 requires Java 25.
patterns.libraryValue: This is the cleanest way to express PumpkinLib's IO-implementation selection: one sealed `HardwareSpec` hierarchy, one factory switch, and adding a vendor becomes a compile-error-driven checklist instead of a silent runtime fallback. It also directly replaces the `if (Constants.currentMode == REAL) new XIOTalonFX(...) else new XIOSim(...)` chain every AdvantageKit project hand-writes in RobotContainer. Caveat: exhaustive switch requires Java 21+, so it is a 2027-and-later feature for FRC (2026 is JDK 17 — sealed interfaces work, pattern-matching switch does not).

patterns.name: Runtime-tunable numbers gated by a global TUNING_MODE flag
patterns.whatItDoes: 6328's `LoggedTunableNumber` publishes gains/setpoints to NetworkTables (3061 uses the `/Tuning` table; AdvantageKit's own docs also say tuning values must publish to `/Tuning` for AdvantageScope) so PID can be adjusted live with no redeploy. A single `TUNING_MODE` boolean in Constants.java flips every tunable between live-editable and hardcoded-constant, so competition builds pay nothing. AdvantageKit's replay-safe primitives are `LoggedNetworkNumber`, `LoggedNetworkBoolean`, `LoggedNetworkString`, `LoggedDashboardChooser<T>(String key)` / `(String key, SendableChooser<T>)` — required because a raw `SmartDashboard.getNumber()` is invisible to replay ('Data retrieved from NetworkTables must be isolated and treated as input data'). Third-party wrapper `TunableControls` wraps WPILib `PIDController`/`ProfiledPIDController` in LoggedTunableNumbers. DogLog also lists tunable values as a first-class feature.
patterns.whereSeen: https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/dashboard-inputs/ ; https://github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib/blob/main/README.md (TUNING_MODE, /Tuning paths, AdvantageScopeTuning.json layout) ; https://github.com/hammerheads5000/TunableControls ; https://doglog.dev/getting-started/faq (tunable values: yes)
patterns.libraryValue: For a small team this is the highest ROI feature in the whole library — deploy cycles are the real bottleneck in-season, and a 30-second redeploy per gain change is why small teams ship untuned mechanisms. PumpkinLib should make EVERY config field tunable-by-default when a tuning flag is on, keyed automatically by mechanism name, with zero extra code from the user. Ship an AdvantageScope layout JSON alongside (3061 ships AdvantageScope.json AND AdvantageScopeTuning.json) so tuning is one file-open, not a manual dashboard build.

patterns.name: Superstructure / coordinating state machine above the subsystems
patterns.whatItDoes: A single class above the per-mechanism subsystems owns cross-mechanism sequencing so no command group has to. 254 2025: `SuperstructureStateMachine` with three top-level modes (CORAL, ALGAECLIMB, CORALMANUAL) plus `ModalControls` to switch driver behaviors, plus a `CoralStateTracker` tracking a game piece through intake→indexer→claw→staged, and `factories/` holding command factories for subsystem coordination. 2910 2026: `Superstructure` lives inside `subsystems/` and 'coordinates robot action'. 254 2023 (pre-AdvantageKit): every subsystem was a singleton extending an abstract `Subsystem` with `readPeriodicInputs()`/`writePeriodicOutputs()`/enabled-loop, driven by a `SubsystemManager`. Spectrum 3847 takes the opposite tack — Triggers-as-states 'all but eliminates the need for complex multi-mechanism command groups.'
patterns.libraryValue: Every top team ends up with exactly one coordination layer; the disagreement is only whether it's an explicit state machine (254/2910) or a trigger web (3847). PumpkinLib should NOT ship an opinionated superstructure — but it should make mechanisms superstructure-friendly: expose `Trigger atPosition(…)`, `Trigger atVelocity(…)`, `Trigger stalled()` factories (3847 does exactly this) and `Command`-returning goal setters, which is the common substrate both styles build on. Also copy the 254 package split: `<team>.lib.*` (reusable, year-independent) vs `<team>.frc20XX.*` (disposable) — that boundary is what makes a library extractable at all.

patterns.name: Commands v3: WPILib's own 2027 'Mechanism' model built on Java continuations
patterns.whatItDoes: New framework in `org.wpilib.commands3`, shipping for 2027 because it needs JVM continuations from Java 21 that the roboRIO could not provide. Commands are written as ordinary sequential method bodies `void commandBody(Coroutine coroutine)`; `coroutine.yield()` returns control to the scheduler, with variants for yield-until-condition and wait-for-duration, so loops and branching read as normal imperative code instead of decomposed initialize/execute/isFinished. `coroutine.await(otherMechanism.someCommand())` composes commands without the parent having to declare the inner mechanism's requirement. The design doc uses the noun **mechanism** (not subsystem) for the exclusively-owned resource; mechanisms have default commands that can be scoped globally, per-opmode, or per-command; commands carry a PRIORITY so a higher-priority command cannot be interrupted by a lower one. Reported layering: imperative API → declarative API → imperative-with-async/await → state machine API. Commands v2 survives in 2027 but with `Command.schedule()` deprecated and RamseteCommand/control commands removed.
patterns.whereSeen: https://github.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/blob/main/design-docs/commands-v3.md ; https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html ; https://github.wpilib.org/allwpilib/docs/2027/java/org/wpilib/commands3/Coroutine.html (javadoc for Command.html 404'd at fetch time; Coroutine URL surfaced in search) ; discussion thread https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/wpilib-commands-v3-imperative-function-bodies-with-coroutines/500699 (NOT fetchable — CD returns 403)
patterns.libraryValue: Decisive for PumpkinLib's naming and timing. WPILib itself is standardizing on 'Mechanism' as the unit of exclusive ownership in 2027 — building PumpkinLib around a `Mechanism` abstraction aligns with, rather than fights, the platform. Concretely: keep the mechanism's requirement/ownership surface thin and adapter-shaped so one core can expose a v2 `SubsystemBase` facade for 2026 and a v3 mechanism facade for 2027. The coroutine `await` model also removes most of the reason to ship your own sequencing helpers — do not invest in command-group utilities that v3 obsoletes. Priority-based interruption is a genuinely new capability worth designing mechanism 'goals' around.

patterns.name: Vendordep distribution: authoritative JSON schema + anonymous-Maven hosting
patterns.whatItDoes: GradleRIO consumes a standalone JSON in the project's `vendordeps/` folder that fully describes the Maven coordinates. Authoritative field list (from the validator, not prose docs): REQUIRED `fileName`, `name`, `version`, `uuid` (valid UUID), `mavenUrls` (non-empty array), `jsonUrl`, `javaDependencies`, `cppDependencies`, `jniDependencies`. OPTIONAL `frcYear` (deprecated) / `wpilibYear` (preferred for 2026+) — **exactly one must be present, never both, never neither**, must start with a digit, and for wpilibYear ≥ 2026 the parent directory in vendor-json-repo must match it. Also optional: `requires[]` and `conflictsWith[]`, each entry {uuid, errorMessage, offlineFileName, and onlineUrl for `requires` only}. javaDependency = {groupId, artifactId, version}. jniDependency adds {isJar, validPlatforms[], skipInvalidPlatforms, simMode}. cppDependency adds {libName (required), configuration, headerClassifier, sourcesClassifier, binaryPlatforms[], sharedLibrary, simMode}. Install online by URL, or CLI `./gradlew vendordep --url=<url>` (local file: `--url=FRCLOCAL/Filename.json`). Listing in the official picker = PR to wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo adding `YEAR/NAME-VERSION.json` plus a `YEAR_metadata.json` entry {name, uuid, description, website, optional instructions} and a `YEAR.json` manifest entry {path, name, version, uuid, description, website, languages:["cpp","java"], instructions?}.
patterns.whereSeen: Schema from validator: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo/main/check.py ; repo + bundle dirs (2024…2026, 2026beta, 2027_alpha1, 2027_alpha5): https://github.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo ; docs https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/vscode-overview/3rd-party-libraries.html ; native template https://github.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-template ; live examples: AdvantageKit https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/releases/latest/download/AdvantageKit.json , DogLog https://doglog.dev/vendordep.json , YAGSL https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/yagsl.json , photonlib 2027-alpha https://maven.photonvision.org/repository/internal/org/photonvision/photonlib-json/1.0/photonlib-json-1.0.json
patterns.libraryValue: For a pure-Java PumpkinLib the whole distribution problem collapses to: publish a jar to an anonymously-readable Maven, then serve one static JSON at a stable URL. Two proven zero-infrastructure hosts, both verified live: (1) **JitPack** — DogLog ships `"mavenUrls": ["https://jitpack.io"]` with `com.github.jonahsnider:doglog`, i.e. tag a GitHub release and JitPack builds it, no Maven account at all; (2) **GitHub Pages as a static Maven repo** — YAGSL serves `https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/releases/` from the same repo that serves its vendordep JSON. AdvantageKit instead uses WPI's own Artifactory (`https://frcmaven.wpi.edu/artifactory/littletonrobotics-mvn-release/`). Also copy YAGSL's use of `mavenUrls` to add `https://repo1.maven.org/maven2` so a Maven-Central transitive dep (dyn4j) resolves, and its `requires[]` block to hard-fail with a readable message when a prerequisite vendordep is missing.

patterns.name: Annotation-driven logging as boilerplate elimination (Epilogue / @AutoLogOutput / DogLog)
patterns.whatItDoes: Three competing approaches to 'log this without writing log calls'. WPILib **Epilogue**: `@Logged` on a class logs every non-static field (public or private) and every public no-arg accessor returning a loggable type; `@NotLogged` opts out; annotation-processor based, no reflection at runtime. AdvantageKit **@AutoLogOutput**: on private/public fields OR getters, supports all types incl. arrays, `StructSerializable`/`ProtobufSerializable`/`WPISerializable`, enums (with `forceSerializable`), and `Measure` with full unit metadata; supports dynamic keys via `{fieldName}` interpolation e.g. `@AutoLogOutput(key = "Module{index}/Speed")`. **DogLog**: rejects annotations/reflection entirely — 'you just call `DogLog.log()` and the value gets logged'; built on WPILib `DataLogManager` + NT4; supports tunables and unit metadata; gives up replay.
patterns.libraryValue: For a small-team library, DogLog's positioning is the closest analogue to PumpkinLib's thesis and worth studying as a competitor: it won adoption (Spectrum 3847 uses it in 2026) by explicitly trading replay for zero ceremony. Design implication: make PumpkinLib's logging PLUGGABLE rather than picking a side — a thin `TelemetrySink` interface with AdvantageKit, DogLog, and Epilogue/NT adapters — because logging framework choice is the most religious decision in FRC and hard-wiring one halves your addressable users. Note that 254 and 3061 use AdvantageKit while 3847 uses DogLog; both camps are large.

patterns.name: maple-sim: physics-backed mechanism/robot simulation
patterns.whatItDoes: Java FRC sim library integrating dyn4j (2D rigid-body dynamics) to simulate forces and collisions between robots, field elements, and game pieces. Provides `SwerveDriveSimulation`, `SwerveModuleSimulation`, `GyroSimulation`, `IntakeSimulation`. 2026 release targets WPILib 2026.2.1 and the REBUILT field. Marketed for testing autos with real accuracy, tuning pathfinding auto-align, and optimizing shooters/subsystems against simulated physics.
patterns.whereSeen: https://github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/maple-sim ; https://shenzhen-robotics-alliance.github.io/maple-sim/ ; https://github.com/Shenzhen-Robotics-Alliance/YAGSL-maple-sim ; integrated in Spectrum 3847's spectrumLib/swerve (MapleSim integration) and depended on by their 2026 robot
patterns.libraryValue: The reason the IO pattern pays off for a SMALL team is not replay — it's that `XIOSim` lets you develop a mechanism before it's built, which is exactly the small-team bottleneck (one robot, no practice bot, limited shop time). PumpkinLib should auto-generate a credible sim IO from the same config that drives the real IO: WPILib already provides `ElevatorSim`/`SingleJointedArmSim`/`FlywheelSim` and the config already carries gearing, `DCMotor` gearbox, mass/MOI, and limits — every input those sims need. That means 'define an elevator once, get a working simulation for free' with no extra user code, which no library currently delivers.

painPoints.problem: The IO-layer pattern costs 4-6 files and several hundred lines per mechanism, all of it mechanical. A single swerve module needs ModuleIO + ModuleIOInputs + generated ModuleIOInputsAutoLogged + ModuleIOSim + ModuleIOTalonFX (+ModuleIOSpark) + Module.java, before any robot-specific logic exists.
painPoints.evidence: AdvantageKit template file inventory at https://github.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/tree/main/template_projects/sources — separate spark_swerve and talonfx_swerve trees each with ModuleIO/ModuleIOSim/ModuleIO<vendor>/Module/GyroIO/GyroIOSim/GyroIO<vendor>/Drive. AdvantageKit's own docs concede the templates are the starting point and say manual project updates are 'not recommended due to the risk of subtle breaking changes' (https://docs.advantagekit.org/whats-new/). DogLog exists specifically as the low-ceremony alternative and won real adoption (https://doglog.dev/getting-started/faq). Search results characterize the templates as 'cumbersome to read'. Reported reception detail from Chief Delphi could NOT be verified — chiefdelphi.com returned HTTP 403 on every fetch.
painPoints.libraryFix: Ship the IO interface + inputs + sim impl + TalonFX impl + Spark impl for a fixed set of archetypes (linear/elevator, rotational/arm/pivot, continuous/roller/flywheel, absolute-encoder turret). A team writes ONE config value and gets the whole stack. Keep the generated IO surface public and subclassable so a team that needs a weird sensor overrides one method instead of forking. This is the core product.

painPoints.problem: Flat `public static final` constants files cannot express two of the same mechanism, cannot be passed as values, cannot be validated, and force copy-paste-and-rename for a second instance. The most-copied template in FRC does exactly this.
painPoints.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Mechanical-Advantage/AdvantageKit/main/template_projects/sources/spark_swerve/src/main/java/frc/robot/subsystems/drive/DriveConstants.java — 40+ loose statics including per-corner duplicated fields (`frontLeftDriveCanId`, `backLeftDriveCanId`, `frontRightDriveCanId`, `backRightDriveCanId`, `frontLeftZeroRotation`, …) and parallel real/sim gain pairs (`driveKp`/`driveSimP`, `turnKp`/`turnSimP`) — the sim-vs-real split is handled by NAMING, not by types. Consumed via `import static ...DriveConstants.*` in Module.java, so the module cannot be instantiated with different constants.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make config a first-class immutable VALUE (record) passed to the constructor, never a static import. Provide `withX()` copy-methods so a second instance is `base.withCanId(7).withInverted(true)`. Provide a single `MechanismConfig` that carries BOTH real and sim parameters so the real/sim split is a field, not a naming convention — and validate in the compact constructor (throw with the mechanism name in the message).

painPoints.problem: Deploy-directory JSON config trades compile-time safety for a debugging experience the library's own docs call unreliable, and silently mis-configured values produce behavior teams cannot diagnose.
painPoints.evidence: YAGSL docs state configuring a swerve module 'is EXTREMELY IMPORTANT and requires a lot of patience and you will likely never get it working on the first try' and 'if one of these configuration values are not set correctly you might experience behavior that you won't easily be able to identify' (https://docs.yagsl.com/configuring-yagsl/configuration/swerve-module-configuration). Symptom examples in docs: wrong module locations vs gyro orientation, device configs in the wrong module file, mandatory per-module `conversionFactor` when one module's motor differs. The community's answer is an out-of-band repo of known-good configs (https://github.com/BroncBotz3481/YAGSL-Configs) — i.e. the format itself doesn't help you get it right. Counterweight: YAGSL's real wins are genuine — one-line construction and 'your constants file doesn't have to take 10 minutes to find the right option' (https://docs.yagsl.com/).
painPoints.libraryFix: Take the wins without the format: (1) ship typed PRESETS as Java constants (MK4i L1/L2/L3, MAXSwerve, common gearboxes) so the 'known-good config' repo becomes an import; (2) per-robot config selection via a subclass/enum (3061 pattern) rather than a directory; (3) validate the entire config graph at construction and fail with mechanism name + field + expected range; (4) log the resolved config as a struct into the WPILOG (StructGenerator.genRecord) so the introspectability benefit of JSON is preserved. If deploy JSON is offered at all, make it a thin deserializer onto the same record — never the primary path.

painPoints.problem: GitHub Packages is unusable for distributing an FRC library — its Maven registry requires an access token even for PUBLIC packages, and GradleRIO consumers have no way to authenticate.
painPoints.evidence: GitHub docs: 'You need an access token to publish, install, and delete private, internal, and public packages' and only ghcr.io (containers) allows anonymous access — https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-apache-maven-registry ; long-running community threads confirming no anonymous Maven read, e.g. https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/38939 and https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/172571. Corroborated negatively by the ecosystem: NO major FRC vendordep uses GitHub Packages — DogLog uses jitpack.io, YAGSL uses GitHub Pages + repo1.maven.org, AdvantageKit uses frcmaven.wpi.edu Artifactory, PhotonVision self-hosts Nexus at maven.photonvision.org.
painPoints.libraryFix: Pick JitPack (zero infra: tag a release, `com.github.<user>:<repo>:<tag>`, mavenUrls `["https://jitpack.io"]` — exactly DogLog's setup) or a GitHub-Pages static Maven repo published by `maven-publish` into `docs/releases/` (exactly YAGSL's setup, and it lets you serve the vendordep JSON from the same Pages site at a stable URL). Decide this on day one because `jsonUrl` and `mavenUrls` must remain stable forever — GradleRIO re-resolves them.

painPoints.problem: AdvantageKit's `@AutoLogOutput` will silently not log anything owned by a third-party library, because discovery is package-scoped to the Robot class's package tree.
painPoints.evidence: https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-outputs/annotation-logging/ — 'Parent class must be in the same package as Robot or a subpackage (unless AutoLogOutputManager.addPackage() is called)' and 'the parent class where @AutoLogOutput is used must also be instantiated within the first loop cycle and discoverable through recursive field searching from Robot.' A library in `org.pumpkinlib.*` satisfies neither condition by default. Separately, installing AdvantageKit requires the consumer to hand-edit build.gradle to add the annotation processor — it is NOT delivered by the vendordep (the vendordep's javaDependencies lists only `org.littletonrobotics.akit:akit-java`).
painPoints.libraryFix: If PumpkinLib emits AdvantageKit outputs, call `AutoLogOutputManager.addPackage("<pumpkinlib root>")` from library init so users never hit the silent-no-op. If PumpkinLib uses `@AutoLog` on its own IO inputs classes, the consumer's build.gradle MUST contain `annotationProcessor "org.littletonrobotics.akit:akit-autolog:$version"` — a vendordep cannot add that, so either document it loudly in `instructions` (the vendor-json-repo metadata supports an `instructions` URL key) or avoid `@AutoLog` entirely and hand-write toLog/fromLog inside the library.

painPoints.problem: The 2027 season is a hard break that will invalidate large parts of any library written against 2026 today.
painPoints.evidence: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html — Java packages `edu.wpi.first` → `org.wpilib`; C++ `frc::` → `wpi::`; Java 25 / C++23 required; roboRIO → Systemcore ('biggest control system update since the introduction of the cRIO'); Shuffleboard, SmartDashboard, PathWeaver, RobotBuilder discontinued; NT3 removed; `robotInit()` removed; `MotorController::set()` → `setThrottle()`; individual gamepad classes collapsed into one `Gamepad`; `Rotation2d` value field removed; `Pose2d/3d.exp(Twist)` → `plus(Twist.exp())`; JSON lib Jackson → Avaje Jsonb; Gradle 9.4.1 + ZGC; removed HAL features incl. Relay, analog output, SPI, DMA, interrupts, counter, ultrasonic, analog trigger, Servo, legacy SPI IMUs. Vendordep schema also changed: `frcYear` deprecated in favor of `wpilibYear` (validator: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo/main/check.py), and platform triples changed (`linuxathena` → `linuxsystemcore`, verified live in photonlib's 2027-alpha JSON). AdvantageKit's main branch ALREADY imports `org.wpilib.math.geometry.Rotation2d`.
painPoints.libraryFix: (1) Never reference Shuffleboard/SmartDashboard — use NetworkTables/DataLog/Epilogue directly. (2) Never touch removed HAL features (Relay, SPI, DMA, counters, Servo, analog trigger) — CAN devices and DIO only. (3) Keep all WPILib imports behind a thin internal seam so the `edu.wpi.first`→`org.wpilib` rename is a mechanical sed on a small surface. (4) Plan two release lines from the start (2026 / 2027) with a shared core, and plan the vendordep JSON to switch `frcYear`→`wpilibYear`. (5) Prefer building the mechanism abstraction so it can front Commands v3, since v3 already uses 'Mechanism' as its core noun.

painPoints.problem: Tuning requires a redeploy unless the team has already built tunable-number infrastructure — which is precisely the infrastructure small teams don't have time to build.
painPoints.evidence: 3061-lib documents this as a headline feature: set `TUNING_MODE = true` in Constants.java to get real-time PID adjustment under `/Tuning` in AdvantageScope 'without recompilation' (https://github.com/HuskieRobotics/3061-lib/blob/main/README.md). AdvantageKit requires replay-safe wrappers (`LoggedNetworkNumber`, `LoggedDashboardChooser`) because raw `SmartDashboard.getNumber()` breaks replay (https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/dashboard-inputs/). A separate third-party library exists purely to wrap PIDController in tunables (https://github.com/hammerheads5000/TunableControls), and DogLog lists tunables as a headline feature (https://doglog.dev/getting-started/faq) — three independent reinventions of the same missing primitive.
painPoints.libraryFix: Make tunability automatic: every numeric field of a mechanism config is published under `/Tuning/<MechanismName>/<field>` when a global tuning flag is on, re-applied to hardware on change, and compiled to a plain constant when off. Ship the AdvantageScope layout JSON so tuning is open-a-file, not build-a-dashboard (3061 ships both AdvantageScope.json and AdvantageScopeTuning.json).

painPoints.problem: Every team re-implements the same ~25 hardware config primitives (gearing, soft limits, supply/stator current limits, gravity type, brake/coast, continuous wrap, follower setup) and the same mechanism utilities (once-per-loop sensor caching, at-setpoint tolerance checks, disconnect alerts, homing).
painPoints.evidence: Spectrum 3847's Mechanism.Config implements all of them by hand: configGearRatio, configForwardSoftLimit, configReverseSoftLimit, configSupplyCurrentLimit, configStatorCurrentLimit, configForward/ReverseTorqueCurrentLimit, configLowerSupplyCurrentLimit/Time, configGravityType(Arm_Cosine vs Elevator_Static), configNeutralBrakeMode, configContinuousWrap, configPeakOutput, configNeutralDeadband, configVoltageCompensation, configFeedbackSensorSource, setFollowerConfigs (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Spectrum3847/2026-Spectrum/main/src/main/java/frc/spectrumLib/mechanism/Mechanism.java). 254 re-implements the same territory differently via ServoMotorSubsystem + tolerance-based `.until()` blocking commands. 3061 re-implements current limiting and system tests again. AdvantageKit's Module.java hand-writes disconnect Alerts per motor.
painPoints.libraryFix: This is the commodity layer — absorb it once, per archetype, with the right defaults baked in (e.g. gravity type is DERIVED from archetype: Arm→Arm_Cosine, Elevator→Elevator_Static; continuous wrap is derived from 'is this a continuous rotation joint'). Ship disconnect Alerts, at-setpoint Triggers, stall detection, and homing routines as standard equipment rather than per-team hand-rolls. Deriving vendor knobs from archetype + physical description is the concrete way to make config shorter than the vendor's own config object.

painPoints.problem: Units API has a real GC footgun and an aliasing footgun that will bite a library that uses it carelessly in periodic code.
painPoints.evidence: https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/basic-programming/java-units.html — 'Immutable arithmetic creates objects constantly… For loops calling these operations repeatedly will stress garbage collection'; and on MutableMeasure, 'Special care needs to be taken when mutating a measure because it will change the value every place that instance is referenced.' Loop overruns from GC are named explicitly as the motivation for MutableMeasure. Corroborating industry practice: Spectrum 3847 pre-allocates all Phoenix control request objects as config fields specifically 'to avoid GC pressure', and caches CAN reads in a `CachedDouble` updated once per loop.
painPoints.libraryFix: Use immutable `Measure` freely in CONFIG (construction-time, allocation is irrelevant) and never in the periodic hot path — convert config to raw base-unit doubles once in the constructor and store those. Follow WPILib's stated API rule verbatim: accept `Measure` in public signatures, return concrete immutable types (`Distance`, never `MutDistance`), and never expose a Mut* type across a library boundary. Pre-allocate all vendor control-request objects at construction.

painPoints.problem: Vendordep dependency chains are brittle and version-churny; a library that depends on other vendordeps inherits every one of their breaking changes and their users' install errors.
painPoints.evidence: YAGSL's live vendordep declares FIVE hard `requires` entries — REVLib, Phoenix6, Phoenix5, Studica, ThriftyLib — each with an errorMessage and a pinned onlineUrl, several pointing at beta artifacts (`Phoenix6-replay-frc2026-beta-latest.json`, `StudicaLib-2026.0.1-beta.json`) (https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/yagsl.json). The 2027_alpha5 bundle already contains FOUR REVLib alphas (alpha2/3/4/6) and two ThriftyLib alphas within one bundle (https://github.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo/tree/main/2027_alpha5), showing the churn rate. GradleRIO also expires online-installed deps: reconnection is required every 30 days or the cache is cleared (https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/vscode-overview/3rd-party-libraries.html).
painPoints.libraryFix: Minimize hard vendor dependencies. Structure PumpkinLib as a vendor-agnostic core (depends on WPILib only) plus OPTIONAL adapter artifacts per vendor, so a REV-only team never needs Phoenix installed. Use `requires[]` with clear errorMessages only for adapters that genuinely need them. Every vendor dependency you add multiplies your install-failure surface and your release cadence obligations.

constraints: PURE JAVA, ZERO JNI — this is the single most important architectural constraint. A pure-Java vendordep needs only `javaDependencies` with empty `jniDependencies`/`cppDependencies` (verified: DogLog https://doglog.dev/vendordep.json, YAGSL https://yet-another-software-suite.github.io/YAGSL/yagsl.json, ThriftyLib). Going native means adopting the 3-library wpilibsuite/vendor-template structure (java lib / C-symbols-only driver lib with an explicit symbols.txt / native C++ lib), cross-compiling for 4-5 platform triples, and re-cutting binaries when the platform set changes — which it JUST did for 2027 (`linuxathena` → `linuxsystemcore`, confirmed in photonlib's 2027-alpha JSON). https://github.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-template

MAVEN HOST MUST ALLOW ANONYMOUS READ. GitHub Packages Maven requires a token even for public artifacts (https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-apache-maven-registry) — disqualified. Proven-viable, verified live: JitPack (`https://jitpack.io`, DogLog), GitHub Pages static Maven (`https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/releases/`, YAGSL), self-hosted Nexus (PhotonVision), WPI Artifactory (AdvantageKit). `jsonUrl` and `mavenUrls` must be permanently stable — GradleRIO re-resolves them on every build.

VENDORDEP JSON REQUIRED FIELDS (from the validator, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wpilibsuite/vendor-json-repo/main/check.py): fileName, name, version, uuid (valid UUID format), mavenUrls (non-empty), jsonUrl, javaDependencies, cppDependencies, jniDependencies. EXACTLY ONE of `frcYear` (deprecated) or `wpilibYear` (preferred, 2026+) — never both, never neither, must start with a digit; for wpilibYear >= 2026 the vendor-json-repo parent directory must equal the value. So a 2026 release carries `"frcYear": "2026"` (AdvantageKit 26.0.2) or `"wpilibYear": "2026"`, and a 2027 release carries `"wpilibYear": "2027_alpha5"` (DogLog, photonlib).

ONE VENDORDEP JSON PER (LIBRARY VERSION x WPILIB YEAR). Because the year is baked into the JSON and validated against the bundle directory, supporting 2026 and 2027 simultaneously means two JSON files at two URLs and two published artifact lines. Plan the branch/release structure for this before the first release.

JAVA LANGUAGE LEVEL: WPILib 2026 = JDK 17 (records ✔, sealed interfaces ✔, pattern-matching switch ✘). WPILib 2027 = Java 25 required (everything ✔, plus the continuations Commands v3 depends on). A library that must run on both is capped at Java 17 syntax for shared code. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/zero-to-robot/step-2/wpilib-setup.html and https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

DO NOT DEPEND ON Shuffleboard, SmartDashboard, PathWeaver, or RobotBuilder — all four are discontinued in 2027. Use NetworkTables, DataLogManager/WPILOG, Epilogue, or AdvantageScope-compatible output only. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/latest/docs/yearly-overview/yearly-changelog.html

DO NOT USE HAL FEATURES REMOVED IN 2027: Relay, analog output, SPI (incl. legacy SPI IMUs ADIS16448/ADIS16470/ADXL345/ADXRS450), analog gyro, DMA, digital glitch filter, interrupts, counter, ultrasonic, analog trigger, Nidec Brushless, Servo, Jaguar, NT3, Axis Camera. Restrict hardware support to CAN devices and DIO. Same source.

ISOLATE WPILIB IMPORTS BEHIND A NARROW SEAM. The 2027 rename `edu.wpi.first.*` → `org.wpilib.*` (C++ `frc::` → `wpi::`) touches every file that imports WPILib. AdvantageKit's main branch has already migrated (its ModuleIO.java imports `org.wpilib.math.geometry.Rotation2d`). Also breaking in 2027: `robotInit()` removed (use the Robot constructor), `MotorController::set()` → `setThrottle()`, all gamepad classes collapsed into one `Gamepad`, `Rotation2d` value field removed, `Pose2d/3d.exp(Twist)` → `plus(Twist.exp())`, `ChassisAccelerations` added, Jackson → Avaje Jsonb, Gradle 9.4.1 + ZGC.

IF USING @AutoLog: the consumer's build.gradle must contain `annotationProcessor "org.littletonrobotics.akit:akit-autolog:$akitJson.version"` — a vendordep CANNOT install an annotation processor. IF USING @AutoLogOutput from library code: call `AutoLogOutputManager.addPackage("<your.root.package>")` at init, or it silently logs nothing because discovery only walks the Robot class's package tree. https://docs.advantagekit.org/getting-started/installation/existing-projects/ and https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-outputs/annotation-logging/

LOGGING FRAMEWORK MUST BE PLUGGABLE, NOT HARD-WIRED. The ecosystem is genuinely split — 254 and 3061 use AdvantageKit; Spectrum 3847 uses DogLog; WPILib pushes Epilogue. Hard-wiring one halves the addressable audience. A thin sink interface with adapters is the only safe choice.

UNITS AT CONFIG BOUNDARIES ONLY, NEVER IN THE HOT LOOP. WPILib's own rules: accept `Measure` in signatures, return concrete immutable types (`Distance`, not `MutDistance`), use `.in(Unit)` only when bridging to non-units APIs, and never expose a mutable measure across an API boundary (mutating one changes it everywhere it's referenced). Convert to base-unit doubles once at construction. https://docs.wpilib.org/en/stable/docs/software/basic-programming/java-units.html

REPLAY-SAFETY: any value read from NetworkTables (including tunable numbers and dashboard choosers) must be routed through a replay-aware wrapper or it breaks AdvantageKit replay determinism ('Data retrieved from NetworkTables must be isolated and treated as input data'). Tunables must publish under `/Tuning` for AdvantageScope compatibility. AdvantageKit 2026 also added a guard that refuses to run replay with HAL simulation extensions loaded. https://docs.advantagekit.org/data-flow/recording-inputs/dashboard-inputs/

MINIMIZE HARD VENDORDEP DEPENDENCIES. Every entry in `requires[]` is an install step and a version-churn liability for the user (YAGSL requires 5: REVLib, Phoenix6, Phoenix5, Studica, ThriftyLib). Split into a WPILib-only core plus optional per-vendor adapter artifacts. Also note GradleRIO clears the online-install cache if the machine doesn't reconnect within 30 days.

NAME THE CORE ABSTRACTION 'Mechanism', NOT 'Subsystem'. WPILib Commands v3 (2027, `org.wpilib.commands3`) uses 'mechanism' as the term for the exclusively-owned resource, adds command priority (higher-priority commands cannot be interrupted by lower), and scoped default commands (global / opmode / command-level). Design the ownership surface thin enough to expose a v2 `SubsystemBase` facade for 2026 and a v3 mechanism facade for 2027. https://github.com/wpilibsuite/allwpilib/blob/main/design-docs/commands-v3.md

UNVERIFIED / OPEN ITEMS, stated explicitly: (1) chiefdelphi.com returned HTTP 403 to every WebFetch attempt (both /t/<slug> and .json forms), so NO Chief Delphi thread content is quoted first-hand anywhere in these findings — community sentiment on AdvantageKit boilerplate, Commands v3, and JSON-vs-Java config remains unconfirmed by primary source. (2) I found NO published FRC library using Java sealed interfaces for hardware/state modeling — that pattern is a proposal here, not an imitable precedent. (3) WPILib's StructGenerator docs do not enumerate which record component types are supported and contain no code examples; whether a `Measure`-typed record component serializes via genRecord is UNKNOWN and must be tested. (4) The rendered WPILib 3rd-party-libraries doc page does NOT document the vendordep schema — the field list above comes from the vendor-json-repo validator source plus live production JSONs, which is authoritative but not officially documented prose. (5) I could not retrieve wpilibsuite/vendor-template's ExampleVendorJson.json (404 on the main branch raw path); the template README was retrieved successfully.
